parameters.query:
-- Every notice DUE and not already logged, one row each. The sender is the real
-- exactly-once guard; this NOT EXISTS only keeps the fan-out small.
--
-- A timed reminder is only due if the booking existed before its window opened: book something
-- for this afternoon and you get a confirmation, not a "reminder" three seconds later telling
-- you what you just did.
--
-- Rows with nobody to send to are left out rather than claimed — an undeliverable notice
-- marked sent is worse than one still pending.
WITH live AS (
  SELECT a.id, a.ref, a.starts_at, a.created_at, a.status, a.stylist_id, a.client_id,
         sv.name AS service_name, sv.duration_min,
         st.name AS stylist_name, st.telegram_chat_id AS stylist_chat,
         c.name  AS client_name,  c.channel_user_id  AS client_chat,
         to_char(a.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'Dy DD Mon, HH24:MI') AS when_local,
         a.starts_at - now() AS lead
  FROM appointment a
  JOIN service sv ON sv.id = a.service_id
  JOIN stylist st ON st.id = a.stylist_id
  JOIN client  c  ON c.id  = a.client_id
  WHERE a.starts_at > now()
), kinds(recipient, kind, needs_status, lead_within, min_notice) AS (
  VALUES ('stylist','booked',       'confirmed', NULL::interval,      NULL::interval),
         ('stylist','reminder_24h', 'confirmed', interval '24 hours', interval '24 hours'),
         ('stylist','reminder_1h',  'confirmed', interval '1 hour',   interval '1 hour'),
         ('client', 'reminder_24h', 'confirmed', interval '24 hours', interval '24 hours'),
         -- A stylist whose diary just lost an appointment needs telling as much as one that
         -- gained one. Without this the chair is quietly empty and nobody knows.
         ('stylist','cancelled',    'cancelled', NULL,                NULL)
)
SELECT d.id AS appointment_id, k.recipient, k.kind,
       CASE
         WHEN k.kind = 'booked' THEN
           format('New booking: %s with %s, %s (%s min). Ref %s.',
                  d.service_name, d.client_name, d.when_local, d.duration_min, d.ref)
         WHEN k.kind = 'cancelled' THEN
           format('Cancelled: %s with %s, %s is no longer going ahead. Ref %s.',
                  d.service_name, d.client_name, d.when_local, d.ref)
         WHEN k.recipient = 'stylist' THEN
           format('Reminder: %s with %s, %s. Ref %s.',
                  d.service_name, d.client_name, d.when_local, d.ref)
         ELSE
           format('Hi %s - a reminder that your %s with %s is %s. Reply here if you need to move it. Ref %s.',
                  d.client_name, d.service_name, d.stylist_name, d.when_local, d.ref)
       END AS text
FROM live d
CROSS JOIN kinds k
WHERE d.status = k.needs_status
  AND (k.lead_within IS NULL OR d.lead <= k.lead_within)
  AND (k.min_notice IS NULL OR d.created_at <= d.starts_at - k.min_notice)
  AND COALESCE(btrim(CASE k.recipient WHEN 'stylist' THEN d.stylist_chat ELSE d.client_chat END), '') <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM notification_log n
        WHERE n.appointment_id = d.id AND n.recipient = k.recipient AND n.kind = k.kind
          AND n.recipient_ref = CASE k.recipient WHEN 'stylist' THEN d.stylist_id ELSE d.client_id END)
ORDER BY d.starts_at, k.recipient, k.kind;

parameters.content:
## 30 · reminders

Every 15 minutes, one question: which notices are **due and not already logged**?

* stylist — `booked` as soon as an appointment exists, then `reminder_24h`, `reminder_1h`, and `cancelled` if it falls through
* client — `reminder_24h`

A timed reminder is only due if the booking existed before its window opened, so a same-day booking gets a confirmation rather than a "reminder" about what you just did. Nobody with no chat id is offered one: an undeliverable notice marked sent is worse than one still pending.

The whole fan-out goes to `39` in ONE call carrying every due item — `39` is multi-item safe, and n8n's per-item mode is deprecated. Exactly-once is `39`'s claim, not this query: two sweeps overlapping still produce one notice each.
